title: Almighty King! Whose Wondrous Hand
description: Almighty King! Whose Wondrous Hand in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: William Cowper wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 515 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Providence of Life”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Al-might-y King! whose won-drous hand Sup-ports the weight of sea and land, Whose grace is such a bound-less store, No heart shall break that sighs for more!

lines: Supports the weight of sea and land,
Whose grace is such a boundless store,
No heart shall break that sighs for more!
And 'tis thy blessing makes it good:
My soul is nourished by thy word;
Let soul and body praise the Lord.
My streams of outward comfort came
From him who built this earthly frame;
Whate'er I want his bounty gives,
By whom my soul forever lives.
Either his hand preserves from pain,
Or, if I feel it, heals again;
From strife and sorrow shields my breast,
Or overrules them for the best.

licence: Public domain: William Cowper died in 1800.
credits: Words by William Cowper (1731–1800), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
